standard_prerequisites: Strong Schmidt subspace theorem, standard Minkowski geometry of numbers and cited Dani correspondence at author granularity
Besicovitch/doubling/good-function and Borel-Cantelli tools as explicitly stated by author
core_obligations: With the strong Schmidt subspace theorem and standard Minkowski/exterior-power tools supplied, the author still builds an eventual rational flag controlling all successive-minimum exponential rates from a subsequence gap, proves stabilization using covolume slopes, and turns the first contracting flag space into a rational totally isotropic projective space through bounded-denominator quadratic pairings. Combining this with Dani correspondence yields the exact algebraic-point exponent and its radical/no-isotropic-subspace cases. This complete flag-to-quadric mechanism is oneH2 result, not a bare citation of Roth or separately counted flag lemma.

the author's own proof environment immediately following the statement: coordinates in the eigenbasis e_{i,x} = u_x^{-1} e_i with the labelled equation (gtv) recording the diagonal action g_t^x v = (e^{-t}v_x^{(1)}, v_x^{(2)}, ..., e^t v_x^{(d)}), then the two directions -- the approximation bound d(x,v) <= H(v)^{-beta} forces |v_x^{(d)}| << ||v||^{-2beta+1} through F = 2x1xd + G, and choosing e^t = ||v||^beta gives gamma(x) >= 1 - 1/beta(x); conversely the contraction ||g_t^x v|| <= e^{-gamma t} forces F(v) = 0 through F(v) = F(g_t^x v), bounds the coordinates through (gtv), and gives d(x,v) << ||v||^{-1/(1-gamma)}, i.e. beta(x) >= 1/(1-gamma(x)) (source lines 291-329)

body_spans.label: the paper's Section 1 setup: the quadrique X = {x in P^{d-1} | F(x) = 0} attached to the rational quadratic form F, the induced height H(v) = max|v_i| on primitive rational points, the projective distance d(x,y) = ||x wedge y||/(||x|| ||y||), and the definition of the exposant diophantien beta(x) as the infimum of the beta > 0 for which d(x,v) >= c H(v)^{-beta} holds with a constant depending on x (source lines 142-158)

body_spans.label: the Section 2 setup for the Dani correspondence: the normal form F = 2x1xd + G(x2,...,x_{d-1}) in a rational basis, the element u_x in O(F) sending x to [e1] given by the theorem of Witt, the diagonal flow g_t^x = diag(e^{-t},1,...,1,e^t) u_x, the systole lambda_1 of a lattice, and the taux de fuite gamma(x) of the orbit g_t^x Z^d, the infimum of the gamma > 0 for which lambda_1(g_t^x Z^d) >= c e^{-gamma t} (source lines 264-281)
